$comment: Canonical AnyFlow design tokens. This file is the single source of truth
for both platforms and is READ BY TESTS on each side, the same way
protocol/testdata keeps the Rust and Kotlin protocol implementations from
drifting. Change a value here and the platform token tests fail until the
Kotlin and Rust/CSS token tables are updated to match.
Two colour families, and the split matters:
brand.*   the identity hues. Fills, marks, gradients, indicator dots.
on_light.* / on_dark.*  the SAME hues corrected to reach WCAG AA as text
and small icons. Brand teal is 2.49:1 on white; it may never
be used for a text label. See docs/design/BRAND.md.

on_light.$comment: Accent hues corrected for text/icon use on white or Paper. All >= 4.5:1 on #FFFFFF.

on_dark.$comment: Accent hues lifted for text/icon use on the dark surfaces. All >= 6.4:1 on #0F172A.

dark.$comment: Derived from Ink rather than inverted: background sits just below Ink, Ink itself is the card surface.

status.$comment: Never carried by colour alone: every status pairs this with an icon and a word. See UI-GUIDELINES.md.

brand.$comment: Decorative only — the ribbon, marks, progress fills. Never put text on it: white on brand teal is 2.49:1.

cta.$comment: The text-bearing gradient. Deepened teal start so white stays >= 4.89:1 at every interpolated point.

progress.$comment: Transfer progress fill. No text sits on it, so the vivid stops are fine.

elevation.$comment: Restrained on purpose: the reference leans on 1px borders and a whisper of shadow, not Material's default lift.

motion.$comment: Flow, not decoration. Every duration here is skipped entirely under reduced-motion.

typography.$comment: Inter where the platform can carry it, otherwise the platform's own UI face, which is metrically close. See BRAND.md.

contrast_floor.$comment: Asserted by the token tests on both platforms. Text must clear AA on its own surface.
